question: The quantities $\ell,c,h$ and $m$ are measured in the units mentioned against each: $\ell$: centimetre; $c$: centimetre per second; $h$: ergs × second; $mc^2$: ergs. Of the expressions $$\alpha=\left(\frac{ch}{m\ell}\right)^{1/2},\quad \beta=\left(\frac{mc}{h\ell}\right)^3,\quad \gamma=\frac{h}{mc\ell},$$ which ones are pure numbers, that is, do not involve any unit?

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level — Sixteenth Edition
